literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) describe a single experimental strategy: the GPI-anchor signal peptide of TNSALP is deleted and replaced with a FLAG-peptide (DYKDDDDK) at the C-terminus. ALPL is a GPI-anchored protein; its only membrane attachment is the GPI anchor. Removing the GPI-anchor signal and substituting FLAG produces a soluble, secreted protein — confirmed explicitly by L2 ('secreted epitope-tagged TNALP') and L4 ('soluble epitope-tagged TNALP… from mouse osteoblast culture supernatant'). The rules require that a qualifying construct be full-length and membrane-anchored; these constructs are neither. They fall squarely under the disqualifying category of 'soluble ectodomain or single-domain construct secreted as a separate protein.' No other insertion modality (fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon screen, bungarotoxin-binding site, HaloTag, etc.) appears anywhere in the ledger for ALPL. Zero sites qualify.
